●

The first 100 levels are to teach the player
all the core gameplay values and strategies
they can form.
Make levels that either rewards mastery or
speed. Make sure to rotate between them
sufficiently for gameplay variety.
Monochromatic and texture heavy levels
should reward speed, whereas levels where
either an item or zombie is being introduced
should reward mastery instead should be a
“no brainer” level.
The approaches can be combined after level
100.

●
●

●

●

Don’t match approaches back to back too
much.
Don’t match more than 2 until level 200
Match 3 sparingly after level 200.
The levels solution should be obvious in the
first glance. That’s not to say levels should
be easy, it just means, on the first look, the
strategy should be obvious, especially for
the first 100 levels. We’ll confuse players
later on after d7 levels by introducing nonobvious levels or trick strategy levels so in
early levels, please avoid these kind of
tricks.

How To Use
Colors?

We have 4 types of color levels. Levels should try to
adhere to these types or use lighter monster track if
using a combination of multiple.

Monochrome
●

●
●
●
●

When making monochrome levels, use objects of the same color that has
at least one other color or detail that’s in another color. Pure color items
are okay, but they shouldn’t exceed 2-3 and should be still visually
distinguishable via shape or texture.
Use monochrome levels sparingly and make sure to rotate between colors.
When making monochromatic levels make sure you choose a middle
saturation unless some textures make it okay to go higher or lower.
Players take a longer time to solve a monochrome level so make sure to
compensate with a more forgiving monster track.
Try to follow with a more forgiving level after a monochromatic level. Aim
to follow up with a level that has items distinguishable through shape and
texture (e.g. like a ball level). At the very least, try to change up the
gameplay style focus.

Complementary Color
Usage
●

When players look at a level made out of complementary colors, they will perceive it as a
whole. Use this to to the levels advantage to steer players towards a certain color via texture

●
●

●

and saturation.
This type of level will get hard in the middle. So make sure your monster track intensifies or
decrease monster track difficulty based on the level difficulty you want. Levels after 70ish are
eligible to support an increase in the middle rhythm in a complementary color level.
Distribution of colors doesn’t really matter. If you have equal amount of the colors, player will
gravitate towards texture and saturation. Same is true if one color is less dominant, therefore
looking more prominent on top of it’s complementary counterpart. Use forced tops and
bottoms if you are concerned about preventing abuse.
Good practice is to use items and details of various sizes for each color. Otherwise the level
will be unfairly difficult and luck will play too much role. If your goal is to create more rhythm
towards the end, you can use similar items but I recommend you force them bottom to create
a nice gameplay shift and layer

.

Analogue
Levels
●
●
●
●
●

Analogue levels are a great alternative to monochrome levels and allow for more flexibility in
item selection.
Analogue levels items should be more or less split equally between colors. If There

is an

imbalance, unlike the complimentary levels, the level will always be a lot more easier.
Analogue levels are great for using the same item of different colors.
If you go for three analogue colors, the third color, either the left one or the right one needs
to become an accent color and have less objects in that color. If you want accent items
without adding another color, go for texture accents.
Neutral colors can always be used as an alternative to a third analogue.

Texture
accent

Example of third
analogue being an
accent

Triad and Tetrad
Levels
●
●
●
●
●

Triad and Tetrad levels should be considered when a noisy level is required for variety.
They can use any triad and tetrad combination and include a neutral, but sparingly.
Neutrals shouldn’t include items the same color as the triad or the tetrad. So if a red shuriken
is present, a gray shuriken shouldn’t be in the level. So it should be avoided in general, but
okay to use sparingly.
Make sure to use textures in such levels.
Use these levels if you want to create levels with similar size items.

Experimental
Levels
●
●
●

Here is an example of an experimental level. It combines a monochrome level with a texture
challenge.
Feel free to throw this kind of level in the funnel to see player reaction for readiness for
mechanic combination etc.
If you have this type of experimental level, make sure it falls in the middle of well learned
passive skills. For example make a level like this after introducing monochromatic levels and
texture challenge levels and There

muscle in both mechanics.

are enough of them for the players to have gained the

The Role of Rhythm in Level Making
●
●
●
●
●

A good level should have a rhythm unique to that level. And a good curve should include variety of level rhythms.
For casual games, avoid using rhythm curves that start fast and slow down over time. Unless you catch a fun one, start slow
and build into it.
The core principle of using rhythm in level making is to make sure the player falls into repetitive motion and gets zoned
out/relaxed while engaging with the content. So as long as this is achieved, your rhythm is working.
Since we’re working with CPM, you can easily test your methods with the level design bot.
You can use rhythm via objects or the monsters, both will work

.

Item Rhythm

●

A good level should have a rhythm unique to that
level. And a good curve should include variety of
level rhythms.

Monster Rhythm
●

A good level should have a rhythm unique to that
level. And a good curve should include variety of
level rhythms.

Core Progression Principles
●

The main principle of the level progression is subjecting players to a certain CPM, and failing
them if they don’t match the speed required.
This requirement begins at very low CPMs until the core game learning curve levels are passed and then
progressively becomes harder, capping at a CPM that will be determined by the data later but projected
to land at 100-120 CPM as a plateau.
As a secondary target, the level durations should also curve and increase over time, eventually reaching
the cap of 90-120 seconds based on the objects of a level.

●
●

Other Considerations
●
●
●

The levels should have zombies reaching the cannon at the target CPM. The logic being, if the players

falls short of the CPM the zombies would pile at the cannon and create urgency.
Try to put zombies at exact times to make sure to achieve this effect, especially in levels that have area
affect items to ensure easier balance.
Level balance target is for players to finish a level without cards, winstreaks, or boosters at
the target CPM.

CPM Targets
1-30 → 50 CPM
30-75 → 60CPM
75-100 ? 70 CPM

100-150 → 75 CPM (will change according to data) = Almost 2 minutes to clear 48 items
150 - onward → 80-90 CPM (will change according to data)

Targets

Levels 5-10 → 25 seconds
Levels 10-15 → 35 seconds
Levels 25-40 → 45 seconds
Levels 40-75 → 60 seconds
Levels 75-100 → 75 seconds
Levels 100-150 → 90 seconds
Levels 150-onward → 90-120 seconds.

3 color scheme max

with occasional

multicolor levels or 4 for item intro
levels.
4-5 quantity (6 max)
5-6 unique items (6 max)
After level 150 we’ll bump this by
1, and CPM by 5 until the
retention data endures the
increased difficulty.

Zombie Lane
Description & Mechanics
Trophy Path is a constant Live-Ops feature that rewards players for achieving certain levels in game play.
Resources
Figma All UI live here.
Rewards Rewards and introduction order lives here.
Icon Behaviour
|  | The icon is displayed on the right corner of the main screen.   The icon is always on top of the list.   The icon displays a red dot, if the player has items to claim within the event.   The progress is visible on the event icon. |
| --- | --- |
The Scene
|  | The scene is a scrollable object.    It always begins at the last achieved milestone and moves as far as the event allows.   The achieved milestones are shown differently than the unachieved ones.   The map icon takes the player to the last unclaimed reward.  The levels players have not achieved are displayed with a dark gray background (see image below). If that level is passed in the main game, they get a golden shield (see image below)   The “i” button displays an infographic.   “X” button takes the player to the main menu. |
| --- | --- |
Container Logic
There are 6 types of containers with different display logic. See backend logic at the bottom of the document for how they translate into UI.
| CONTAINER 0 | Normal milestones with no rewards are showed as Container 0 in the documentation. |
| --- | --- |
| CONTAINER 1 | Displays a single small item. The reward item is in the middle, and the quantity is shown underneath.   The corresponding level is displayed in the bottom left corner of the container.   The bottom right portion of the container displays a “Claim” button if the reward is still unclaimed, and a green tick symbol for the claimed rewards.     Displays 2 small items. Same UI, display and claim button state rules apply |
| --- | --- |
| CONTAINER 2 | Displays 3 small items. Same UI, display and claim button state rules apply. |
| --- | --- |
| CONTAINER 3 | Displays 4 small items. Same UI, display and claim button state rules apply. |
| --- | --- |
| CONTAINER 4 | Displays 1 large item. Same UI, display and claim button state rules apply. |
| --- | --- |
| CONTAINER 5 | This container is designated for unlocking. It  displays the unlocked item and a small currency reward.   “I” button displays a pop-up style infographic. (see infographic section for more detail)  Left side displays the “UNLOCK TYPE” item   The right side displays the currency reward and quantity which is nestled at a Reward column prior. |
| --- | --- |
Reward Claim
When a reward becomes available, the player is informed via a red dot on the screen. The red dot shows the number of rewards available for claim. From There, they can enter the Zombie Lane scene and claim their rewards.
Infographic Pop-Ups
Infographic pop-ups are available for certain items via the “i” button.  But we should make the entire panel clickable and will bring up the pop up even if they don’t click on the “i”
|  | Meet&Greet UI is used to introduce zombies in the event.   It has one header, one funny tagline and and an explanation to her ability at the bottom.   “x” exits to Zombie Lane scene. |
| --- | --- |
|  | Unlocked UI is used to display the contents of the item pack.    “x” exits to Zombie Lane scene. |
| --- | --- |
Data Driving
The order of rewards that are displayed in the event will be controlled via an Excel sheet linked in the resources section.
| step | Displays TRUE or FALSE.  If it’s true it means the level will be displayed on the lane.   For instance, if level 8 is TRUE it’s displayed on the lane like this.     If the step is a reward level, the level information is displayed on the container instead of the gray step. |
| --- | --- |
| CONTAINER | If a level has no rewards, meaning it’s just a step, then the container info shows FALSE.  There are 6 container types (see container logic above). If the level has a reward in it, the type of container is displayed here.   For instance level 7 has 2 small rewards which is the  display type of the Container 2. |
| --- | --- |
| REWARD & QUANTITY | There are 4 reward and quantity columns because the rewards can go up to 4. The reward tab displays the name of the object, and the quantity displays the number of rewards being given of that object. |
| --- | --- |
| UNLOCK & UNLOCK TYPE | Some levels have an unlock column. If the level doesn’t have anything to unlock, it shows FALSE. If this is true, it displays what is being unlocked.   For example if a new zombie is being introduced, the unlock column says “Zombie”. Let’s say the Cheerleader zombie is being introduced. Then the UNLOCK TYPE says “Cheerleader” |
| --- | --- |

record.body_text:
Event Icon Management System v1.0
Overview:
The purpose of this system is to create a structure for the LiveOps event icons. This system dictates the following:
The number of icons on a scene
When they will appear whether locked or unlocked
What side of the screen will an icon appear
In what order an icon will appear
When will the icon disappear and/or change places
The various elements on the icon like time, buttons, notifications, etc.
Seasonal changes
What’s in it for [SOURCE_ORG_0451]:
To have an across-prototype transferable Live Operations icon ordering.
Main Workings:
Icon Amount
The main UI can have a maximum of 10 icons on the screen at any given time.
If the situation calls for more icons, both of the columns will shrink in icon size and the slot amount will be increased accordingly.
(add a  screenshot with different resolutions)
Icon Placement By Type
All gameplay-related icons will be showcased on the left side while the monetization icons will appear on the right.
Icon Placement By Announcement (Lock State)
The event icon management system should have the flexibility to add incoming events by level in a locked state.
Locked event icons appear semi-grayed out as seen in the image below.
If we decide to display lock sprites on top of icons, they will display an unlocking animation when the player hits the corresponding level.
When the player reaches the desired level, the lock does a simple bounce animation before shrinking back to its size and getting color.
While the icons are in their lock state, they shouldn’t get any animations.
Write ticket for Marcus to change the lock animation.
The graying out will be done with engineering. It will be not be graying out but the black overlay instead. During this operation, we need to consult with the art team and they will dictate the color of the overlay.
Icon Placement By Order
Monetization Column
The monetization column displays the monetization-related icon with a custom priority. Each icon will have the following attributes:
Sticky
This attribute determines whether the icon will remain in the assigned position at all times until the offer is over.
Initial Starting Position
Each icon will appear on the screen with an initial starting position. This position is always 1 if There are no sticky icons and the slot after the sticky icons if There are any.
This way, any offer will remain sticky for as long as we want it, and all new icons will appear directly under sticky icons. The new icons will naturally take the first slot and others will descend accordingly. So, each time There is a new offer, the icons descend to the next slot.
Gameplay Column
The event icon management system will use the following ruleset:
The screen displays the locked events (if There are any) to begin with.
The screen displays the events as they unlock prioritizing top order.
After all the events have been unlocked, events start queuing.
The queue has the following criteria:
If the game event icon has a panel that opens and closes it always takes the first place and becomes sticky until the event is over. If a second icon has a panel it takes the second place and follows the same rule.
The next priority are the events we tag as sticky.
After that the first try events take their place. They appear in the first slot available when they start and disappear when the event is over.
5. Icon Elements
For the sake of simplicity, each icon will have a ribbon as shown below in the Royal Match example. The text and color of this ribbon will be determined from the code.
Ongoing State (Timer)
The ongoing state of an icon means the player has agreed to start the event via pop-up. After that, the icon will display the timer for the event. For auto-start events, the ongoing state starts immediately. 

The timer follows the standard dd:mm:ss format.
Start State
The start state of an icon means the player has ignored the event and didn’t activate it. In that case, the event will display a “Start” text on the ribbon.
End State
The end state of an icon is triggered in the following scenarios:
The player finished the event but didn’t collect their reward.
The player started the event but didn’t finish it.
Lock State
Only true if we introduce the icons by level. See above for details.
*If the players don’t claim rewards and the event cycle resets, it’s better to show a pop-up in case they don’t click on the “claim” button as well.
Notification System
This system will display different notifications based on the state of the event. The monetization event gets their notifications on the left, whereas the gameplay column gets their notification on the right side of the icon.
Red Dot Notification
The continuation of the red dot notification system we already have.
Green Circle Notification
The green circle shows uncollected rewards.
Leaderboard Notification
Leaderboard notifications are displayed on the icon itself and show the player where they rank within an event.
Discount notification
To be added to monetization icons as needed.
Progress System
The progress system uses the curved progress bar we currently use in the game. Based on the event, the developer will incorporate the progress bar if stated in the spec-specific event.
6. Seasonal Changes
If we decide to make an event season-based, (e.g. Christmas or Halloween edition) the icon will be updated accordingly. Seasonal event icons follow the same rules as the generic icons.
Art:
Icon Skeleton
The icons will use a generic frame, similar to what we have in Domino Delights now. Since Domino Delights uses a more fantasy/female-friendly vibe, we might iterate on it. To be discussed further with the art team.
Rank placeholder is not always an option so design around it.
Iconography
A generic icon library that will be suited for any type of game. All icons will have VFXs that can be grown into other icons as well. So they should be generic. To be discussed with the art team to figure out in the kickoff meeting.
So, I did talk with the art team and they ripped me a new one. No generic icons :P
Art Direction
General suggestions are listed below:
Since the notification colors will be white, green, and red, the icons shouldn’t be using these colors heavily.
All icons should use a similar/same color scheme to look harmonious no matter what.
Since the border size and color will be the same, the icons need to follow complimenting borders, thickness, and color.
The icons should be 2D elements with 3D perspective. This kind of style is called physical touching (don’t call HR)
The ribbons will have the color of the skeleton. (Martin will make a presentation for this)
We are a trendy company
CLAIRE is a Captain Obvious person.
VFX Consideration
The VFXs should be generic and based on manipulation of the shape rather than being icon-specific. To be discussed with the art team whether it’s better to make it code or art-based. 

But for some of the icons, e.g. race flags, we can have them custom made since these icons will be used over multiple prototypes.
Size change
[PERSON_NAME_66179]
Bounce
[USERNAME_12151]
Lock VFX
The unlock VFX we currently have should be adjusted to the generic system. See below.
(low priority) For the ranking events, where the player reaches the top spot, we can add a VFX (TBD) to make it obvious.
After [USERNAME_5509] completes his list and Calvin makes the skeleton prefab, we’ll sync and investigate if adding the generic animations to the prefab makes sense.
I asked [PERSON_NAME_66177] how long this will take. And he told me to mind my own business. (one week not counting animation work including testing)
Future Iterations:
We need a system that allows for an event to be unlocked even if it’s not available that day.
